suggestions.rationale: Chronic hypoparathyroidism is associated with renal complications including nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis, but the relationship can reflect both the underlying calcium-phosphate disorder and its long-term conventional calcium/active-vitamin-D treatment context. A 2022 systematic review supporting the international guideline program identified nephrocalcinosis/nephrolithiasis among the complications probably associated with chronic hypoparathyroidism. This is an association-focused research relationship, not an automatic causal attribution of an individual's kidney stones to hypoparathyroidism.
evidenceGaps: Documentation confirming chronic hypoparathyroidism and its etiology/duration
Longitudinal calcium, phosphate, PTH, magnesium, creatinine/eGFR, and vitamin D results
Calcium and active-vitamin-D treatment history, doses, and duration
24-hour urine calcium and other metabolic stone testing when available
Renal imaging, stone chronology/composition, and clinician review of alternative stone causes

sourceReferences.citation: Yao L, Hui X, Li M, et al. Complications, Symptoms, Presurgical Predictors in Patients With Chronic Hypoparathyroidism: A Systematic Review. J Bone Miner Res. 2022;37(12):2642-2653. PMID 36375810
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review of 93 studies and 18,973 patients identified nephrocalcinosis/nephrolithiasis among complications probably associated with chronic hypoparathyroidism; supports a conservative association-focused kidney-stone research relationship rather than individual causal attribution.
